Syntax: swalk <directions>
              |
              |        Execute a sequence of movements using shorthand notation.
              |        Swalk allows you to move through multiple rooms efficiently
              |        by specifying direction and repetition counts in one command.
              |
              |        Valid directions: n (north), s (south), e (east), w (west)
              |                          u (up), d (down)
              |
              |        Examples:
              |          swalk 2s3eu     = go south twice, then east three times, up once
              |          swalk n ne       = north, northeast (parsed as north then east)
              |          swalk 5u         = up five times
              |
              |        Notes:
              |          - You must be standing to use swalk
              |          - Cannot speedwalk while in combat
              |          - Speedwalk stops immediately if a move fails (locked door, no exit, etc)
              |          - Maximum 100 consecutive moves in one speedwalk
              |          - Directions are not case-sensitive
              |          - Diagonal exits (ne/nw/se/sw) are NOT supported by swalk; use
              |            the full command name (e.g. 'ne' or 'northeast') directly
              |
              |        Related: north, south, east, west, up, down,
              |                 northeast, northwest, southeast, southwest
              |
